subject: Urban Planning
title: Ordos Kangbashi: China's Ghost City
description: A short lesson to help you apply Ordos Kangbashi: China's Ghost City.

hook.text: China built a city for one million people in Inner Mongolia. For years, almost nobody moved there.

buildup.text: Kangbashi had museums, stadiums, and apartment towers. It lacked one thing: reasons for people to come.

discovery.text: China built dozens of ghost cities using real estate as an economic engine. GDP grew; residents didn't come.

twist.text: Kangbashi is slowly filling up — schools, government offices, and subsidies have pulled 100,000 residents in.

climax.text: The lesson: you can build a city, but you can't build a reason to live there. Jobs come first.

punchline.text: Build it and they will come. Eventually. Maybe.

quiz.question: Why did Ordos Kangbashi initially remain empty?
options: Construction defects made the buildings uninhabitable
It had infrastructure but no jobs or reasons for people to move there
Government restrictions prevented citizens from relocating
